en: Indeed, Oak is about combining multiple
middleware functions that might be doing
different things.
One middleware function might extract data
from the incoming request, another function
might prepare the response.
Here, I'll add a second function simply by
repeating app.use,
and I will console.log middleware2 here and
change my message to message from
middleware2.
Now if we save it like this
and we maybe delete these logs,
our server restarts here.
But if I now reload, you will still see
message from middleware 1.
So it doesn't look like our second
middleware ran. We also don't see this log
somewhere down there in the console. We only
see the log from middleware 1 about the URL,
which seems to be this object here,
and about the request method.
The reason for that is that we need to call
next in order to tell Oak that after this
middleware, we wanna forward the incoming
request to the next middleware in line.
And when I say in line, I mean the next
middleware below it because a request
basically travels through your middleware
functions from top to bottom. That is how
you can think about it. So it will first
reach this middleware and if you call next
in there, it will move on to the next
middleware in line. If you don't call next,
this middleware here will not be reached as
you just saw.
Now, if a middleware does not call next, the
response will be sent back.
With that, if we save this
and we reload, we should see message from
middleware 2 here.
Because now the second middleware was
reached and since we set the response body
here as well, we override what we set here
and therefore it's this response body which
is actually sent back to the client. This is
how the middleware functions generally work
here.
Now when Oak is out of middleware functions
that should be processed, it will send the
response back to the client. As long as you
keep on going through middleware functions,
It will continue doing that and the response
will only be sent back once you, well, went
through all the middleware.
